**For most buyers, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** NMC only wins if you need the lightest possible unit and will use it rarely.

**Why LiFePO4 usually wins**

- **Cycle life:** LFP units are typically rated for 3,000 to 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity, while NMC units are typically rated for 500 to 1,000 ([VoltVanguard](https://volt-vanguard.com/article/lifepo4-vs-nmc-battery-chemistry/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Daily use makes this difference matter most: one guide estimates an NMC unit rated at 500 cycles lasts under two years of daily cycling, versus about eight for a 3,000-cycle LFP unit ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed less violently. They ran cooler and released smoke without flames, while the NMC cells in the same test ignited ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). LFP is not fireproof, though, and one source notes LFP systems have had incidents too ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Cost:** The price gap has mostly closed. Per-cycle cost favors LFP because of its longer rating ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC has an edge**

- **Weight:** NMC stores more energy per pound at the cell level, but the gap shrinks in finished units because the inverter, case, and fans weigh the same either way. One database found the median NMC model at 39.2 Wh/lb versus 35.5 Wh/lb for LFP ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).

**Caveats**

- Sources disagree on exact cycle and temperature figures, so compare the specific model's spec sheet.
- Charging limits depend on the manufacturer more than the chemistry. Many LFP units won't charge below 32°F (0°C) ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
